job losses this year were abundant,

Medicine was expensive too...

Though he too would catch the disease.

There was shopping at his feet

To woo a girl, cute and petite

She'd come to him crying though,

For reasons he was scared to know.

The man far to his left was the cause

The head of a buisiness, with tremendous loss,

With a heavy heart he adressed his staff

And said their numbers had to cut in half.

Tears they shed, and he shed them too,

But there was nothing he could do.

He said farewell to each of them in turn,

and hoped one day they could return.

So that is the tale of this dreary train,

Sheltering them for the pouring rain.
